extracted.intended_audience: recipients under Title IX (college/university administrators, Title IX coordinators, institutional legal counsel, policy makers)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for a recipient's Title IX grievance process, including presumptions, neutrality and training, supportive measures, time frames, and evidentiary treatment. Focused on how institutions must design and implement grievance procedures under 34 C.F.R. §106.45 and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility (§106.45(b)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must operate under a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged conduct until a determination regarding responsibility is made at the conclusion of the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is not a statement about the respondent's credibility, believability, or truthfulness; recipients must not prejudge facts or draw inferences about credibility based on party status. The presumption reinforces the recipient's burden of proof and proper application of the standard of evidence and is intended to improve legitimacy and reliability of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No credibility determinations based on party status
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX personnel must refrain from making credibility determinations or drawing conclusions about a party's truthfulness based solely on whether the party is a complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(1)(ii) requires recipients not to make credibility determinations based on a party's status. Personnel should avoid assumptions about either party until the grievance process concludes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal procedural rights while burden rests on recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Both complainants and respondents have equal procedural rights to meaningfully participate in presenting views, evidence, and desired outcomes, while the recipient bears the burden of proof for a determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations ensure parties have equal opportunities (e.g., gathering/presenting evidence) but the recipient retains responsibility to meet the burden of proof; neither party should be deemed to carry that burden during the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and training of Title IX personnel (§106.45(b)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX personnel must serve without bias for or against complainants or respondents and must receive training expressly to avoid such bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have discretion over training content and approaches so long as they meet §106.45(b)(1)(iii) requirements. Training should address avoiding both general and individual bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process neutrality and limits on treating respondents as guilty pre-adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not treat respondents as though accusations are true prior to an adjudication establishing responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations circumscribe recipient discretion to impose disciplinary/punitive actions before factual determination. The presumption of non-responsibility is intended to prevent treating accused persons as responsible until conclusion of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor participation and counsel (limits and permissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisors may be attorneys, but recipients may limit the active participation of advisors except that at postsecondary live hearings advisors conduct cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations permit, but do not require, attorney advisors. Recipients may significantly limit advisor participation except for the right to conduct cross-examination at a live hearing in postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures obligation to complainants (§106.44(a) & §106.30 definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are obligated to offer supportive measures to every complainant, engaging in an interactive process where the Title IX Coordinator discusses available supportive measures, considers complainant wishes, and explains the option to file a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are individualized, without fee or charge, and may be provided before or after filing a formal complaint or where no formal complaint is filed. Title IX Coordinators are responsible for effective implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation when supportive measures are not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient's response to sexual harassment does not include providing supportive measures to a complainant, the recipient must specifically document why that response was not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: document that the complainant refused supportive measures or did not wish to receive them. This documentation requirement is codified in revised §106.45(b)(10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures may not be punitive; must not unreasonably burden other party
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures are designed to restore or preserve equal educational access and cannot be punitive or disciplinary; they also must not 'unreasonably burden' the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures such as changing a respondent's class schedule or forbidding communication may be appropriate if they do not unreasonably burden the respondent. The presumption of non-responsibility does not prohibit providing supportive measures to complainants that meet these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may provide supportive measures to respondents (no obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no obligation to offer supportive measures to respondents, though recipients may provide them; grievance processes must describe the range of supportive measures available to complainants and respondents (§106.45(b)(1)(ix)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should include the range of supportive measures in their grievance procedures; offering supportive measures to respondents is permitted but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal and administrative leave (§106.44(c) & (d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may remove a respondent on an emergency basis when necessary to ensure physical health or safety and may place employees/students on administrative leave; such measures do not preclude continuing the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removal is distinct from supportive measures and allowed under §106.44(c). Administrative leave does not prevent an investigation from proceeding; recipients can facilitate participation remotely or with safety measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No adverse inferences from a party's absence or silence (§106.45(b)(6)(i) revision)
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision-maker cannot draw any inferences about the determination regarding responsibility based on a party's failure to appear at the hearing or answer cross-examination or other questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects Fifth Amendment concerns and prevents a party from being found responsible solely because they declined to testify or participate; applies equally to complainants and respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably prompt time frames for concluding grievance processes (§106.45(b)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance process must include reasonably prompt time frames for concluding the entire grievance process, including appeals and informal resolution processes; temporary delays and limited extensions permitted only for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time frames must be designated and published by the recipient and judged reasonable in context of the recipient's educational operations. Short-term delays/extensions must be for 'good cause' (non-exhaustive factors are provided) and recipients must notify parties of reasons for delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to set time frames but accountability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to select specific time frames (e.g., 60 days or another period) that they determine are reasonably prompt given their circumstances, but they are accountable to meet the time frames they designate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting recipients to choose reasonable time frames tailored to their institution encourages adherence and acknowledges differences in complexity, size, and mission. The recipient should select time frames it can meet in most situations, using short-term extensions for exceptional complexities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on permissible delays and good cause standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Delays caused solely by administrative needs are insufficient to constitute good cause; even where good cause exists delays must be temporary and limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must attempt to accommodate schedules of parties and witnesses, but a party's refusal to cooperate cannot indefinitely delay a proceeding. The grievance process may proceed to conclusion even in absence of a party or witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance promptness with fairness and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must balance the need for reasonably prompt resolution with procedures designed to ensure fairness and reliable outcomes; prompt resolution is necessary to restore equal access but not at the expense of fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures should be implemented during pending processes; remedies after a finding may include measures not permissible as supportive measures. Timeframes should reflect the goal of concluding as quickly as possible while complying with §106.45 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include time frames for all grievance stages (including appeals and informal resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reasonably prompt time frame requirement applies to every stage of a grievance process, explicitly including appeals and any informal resolution processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text was revised to make appeals mandatory and to ensure informal resolution processes (if offered) are also subject to reasonably prompt time frame commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient notification when delaying or extending time frames
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient implements a temporary delay or limited extension for good cause, the recipient must notify the parties of the reason for such delay or extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice requirement preserves transparency and accountability and helps ensure that delays are factually justified and not indefinite.
